exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

Which brand would you recommend for a high-protein snack, and why?
reviewed_answer:
My top recommendation is Good Culture 2% Low-Fat Cottage Cheese. It offers an excellent combination of high protein, creamy texture, simple ingredients, and convenience for snacking.

Good Culture Classic Simply Cottage Cheese, 2% Milk Fat, 19 …

My top pick

Per 5.3 oz single-serving cup

Listed price; local availability may vary.

Why I'd choose Good Culture

High protein: The 5.3-ounce cup provides 19 grams of protein, making it a substantial snack between meals or after exercise.

Simple ingredients: Made with milk, cream, salt, and live cultures, without unnecessary thickeners in its classic formulation.

Enjoyable texture: Thick, creamy, and less watery than many traditional cottage cheeses.

Convenient: The single-serving cup requires no preparation and provides a predictable protein portion.

Well-reviewed flavor: Good Culture has performed particularly well in independent cottage cheese taste tests. 

How it compares with alternatives

Daisy 2% Cottage Cheese Cups

17g protein per 5.3 oz cup

A strong alternative if you prefer a more traditional cottage cheese flavor. Daisy's low-fat version also performed exceptionally well in recent Consumer Reports testing. 
These 2 Came Out on Top

Great Value 2% Cottage Cheese

13g protein per ½ cup

My budget-friendly choice. A large tub offers better value if you're eating cottage cheese regularly.

My favorite way to eat it

Try a cup of Good Culture with fresh blueberries, sliced strawberries, and a few walnuts. It's a quick way to add fiber and healthy fats to an already protein-rich snack.

Bottom line: I'd buy Good Culture 2% in the 5.3-ounce cups if protein, taste, and convenience are the priorities. If you're looking to save money and eat cottage cheese daily, I'd choose a larger tub of Daisy or Great Value instead.

One thing worth checking is sodium: cottage cheese can be relatively salty, so compare the labels if you're watching your intake.
